verdict.summary: Anyone with MFA turned on can create a Connect API integration and test it in draft, but a public integration has to pass Canva review before other Canva users can authorize it, and Canva publishes no review timeline. The no-review alternative, a private integration, only works for your own team on a Canva Enterprise plan; for AI agents the hosted Canva MCP server can be switched on for the same Developer Portal app.

evidence.label: inferred
evidence.note: Enable MFA, create the integration, pick scopes, add an http://127.0.0.1 redirect, and implement PKCE.

timeToProd.assumes: A public integration (Connect REST API or Canva MCP via the Developer Portal) that reads and edits users' designs; a private integration skips review but only serves your own Canva Enterprise team.
timeToProd.waitingOn: Canva's integration review (tracked in a Jira Service Desk ticket; no stated SLA).

evidence.label: inferred
evidence.note: Canva says review duration 'depends on the complexity of the app and the amount of feedback required'. The range is our estimate, not a Canva figure.

verdict.cost: No developer fee found. Brand templates, autofill, brand kits and resize need the end user to be on Canva Pro or above (per the MCP access docs); private integrations need Canva Enterprise.

prerequisites.item: A Canva account with multi-factor authentication enabled
prerequisites.why: Canva requires MFA before you can create an integration.

prerequisites.item: A backend to hold the client secret and PKCE verifier
prerequisites.why: Token requests use HTTP Basic auth with the client ID and secret and can't be made from a browser (CORS); the code verifier must stay hidden from the user's browser.

prerequisites.item: A production HTTPS redirect URL (no local URLs at submission)
prerequisites.why: http://127.0.0.1:<port> works for development (localhost isn't allowed), but public integrations can't be submitted while a local redirect URL is configured.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: The localhost-vs-127.0.0.1 detail came from a Canva docs search snippet; the checklist confirms local redirect URLs block submission.

prerequisites.item: Reviewer test credentials and documentation for your platform
prerequisites.why: The submission checklist asks for a test account login if authentication is used, plus platform documentation.

scopeTiers.impact: No Canva submission, but only usable by your team, and only if that team is on Canva Enterprise.

scopeTiers.tier: Public integration: design, asset, folder, comment scopes
scopeTiers.impact: Any Canva user can authorize after approval. Scopes are explicit: asset:write doesn't imply asset:read.

Only useful for end users on paid plans (Pro and above per the MCP docs). The 2024 launch post said integrations using Autofill and Brand Template endpoints couldn't be submitted yet; current status is unclear.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: The submission restriction is from June 2024 and may be outdated.

scopeTiers.impact: Needs a valid webhook URL configured before submission.

steps.title: Enable MFA on your Canva account
steps.detail: Turn on multi-factor authentication in Canva account settings; it's required to create integrations.

steps.title: Create a public integration in the Developer Portal
steps.detail: Open the Developer Portal, create an integration of type Public (Private needs Enterprise), and copy the client ID and generate a client secret.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: We didn't sign in; portal pages returned 403 to unauthenticated requests.

steps.title: Choose scopes and configure redirect URLs
steps.detail: Pick explicit scopes (e.g. design:content:read, design:meta:read, asset:read, profile:read). Add http://127.0.0.1:<port>/oauth/redirect for development and your HTTPS production URL.

steps.title: Implement Authorization Code + PKCE
steps.detail: Redirect to https://www.canva.com/api/oauth/authorize with client_id, scope, code_challenge (S256, 43–128 char verifier), state and redirect_uri. Exchange the code at POST https://api.canva.com/rest/v1/oauth/token with Basic auth and the code_verifier.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: Token URL path observed live (400 'Content-Type header is missing for /rest/v1/oauth/token').

steps.title: Implement single-use refresh tokens
steps.detail: Access tokens are short-lived. Each refresh token can only be used once and returns a new pair, so persist atomically and serialize refreshes.

steps.title: Optional: turn on Canva MCP for the app
steps.detail: Toggle Canva MCP on in the app's configuration to use the hosted MCP endpoint https://api.canva.com/connect/v1/mcp with the same client credentials.

steps.title: Test in draft with your own account
steps.detail: Authorize, run core flows, and test the auth flow with and without an active Canva session.

steps.title: Prepare submission materials
steps.detail: Remove local redirect URLs, check the app name, draft listing copy, write platform documentation and reviewer notes, and follow the brand, design and security guidelines.

steps.title: Create reviewer test account and submit
steps.detail: Provide test login details, agree to the Developer Terms, and submit from the Developer Portal. You can submit at most 5 times a day, and a submitted app can't be modified without cancelling the submission.

steps.title: Canva review
steps.detail: The integration joins Canva's review queue with a Jira Service Desk ticket for all communication. Duration depends on complexity and feedback rounds.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: Duration is our estimate; Canva gives none.

steps.title: Release
steps.detail: After approval, release the integration so any Canva user can authorize.

agentCanDo: Select explicit scopes and generate redirect/config values
Implement PKCE, state checks and single-use refresh handling
Draft listing copy, platform docs and reviewer instructions
Run the submission checklist (local URLs, webhook URL, app name)
Check OIDC and MCP OAuth metadata endpoints
humanMustDo: Enable MFA and create the integration in the Developer Portal
Generate and store the client secret
Provide a reviewer test account for your service
Submit, respond in the Jira ticket, and release after approval

blockers.symptom: Can't create an integration in the Developer Portal
blockers.cause: MFA isn't enabled on the Canva account.
blockers.fix: Turn on multi-factor authentication, then return to the portal.

blockers.symptom: Submit button blocked or submission rejected over redirect URLs
blockers.cause: A local (127.0.0.1) redirect URL is still configured on a public integration.
blockers.fix: Remove local redirect URLs (keep a separate dev integration for local testing).

blockers.cause: Private integrations need a Canva Enterprise team.
blockers.fix: Use a public integration and go through review, or use an Enterprise team.

blockers.symptom: Refresh fails with an invalid grant after working once
blockers.cause: Canva refresh tokens are single-use; a parallel or retried refresh reused an old token.
blockers.fix: Serialize refreshes per user and persist the new refresh token before using the access token.

evidence.label: inferred
evidence.note: Single-use is documented; the exact error string isn't.

blockers.symptom: Token requests fail from the browser with CORS errors
blockers.cause: Endpoints that need the client secret can't be called from a web-browser client.
blockers.fix: Move the code exchange and refresh to your backend.

blockers.symptom: Brand template or autofill calls fail for some users
blockers.cause: Those features need the user to be on Canva Pro or above.
blockers.fix: Detect the plan and degrade gracefully; don't make them core to your flow.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: Plan tiers stated for MCP; assumed similar for REST.

nuances.text: Canva supports no organization-level authentication for MCP: each user authorizes individually and sees only what their own permissions allow.

Canva MCP has two onboarding routes: self-serve via the Developer Portal (client ID + secret, endpoint api.canva.com/connect/v1/mcp) or a reviewed waitlist for secretless CIMD clients (endpoint mcp.canva.com/mcp). DCR still works but is deprecated in favour of CIMD.
Canva's OIDC uses pairwise subject identifiers, so the user's sub differs per client; don't use it to join users across apps.

evidence.label: tested
evidence.note: subject_types_supported: ["pairwise"] in the discovery document fetched 2026-10-20.

nuances.text: Scopes are explicit and must already be set in the integration's settings; you can't request a scope you haven't configured, and write doesn't imply read.
Once submitted, an integration can't be edited without cancelling the submission, which likely puts it back in the queue.

evidence.label: inferred
evidence.note: Cancel-to-edit is documented; the queue reset is our inference.
